ai.title: Add node >=14 engine requirement to npm-app
ai.summary: Added engines.node >=14 to npm-app/package.json. Enforces minimum Node.js version for the CLI package. Scope limited to npm-app package metadata. npm will warn or fail on install if host Node version is below 14.

eli5.text: When you install this command-line tool, your computer now needs to have a recent enough version of the software platform installed, basically, anything older than version 14 will cause the installation to stop with a warning or an error. This only affects the specific command-line tool in this package; the rest of the program will continue to run normally if your system already meets the requirement. To see if it applies to you, try installing or updating the tool, if your setup is too old, the process will simply tell you to upgrade first.

ai.title: Windows command notes added to system prompt
ai.summary: Windows-specific command notes injected into system prompt for `win32` platforms. Maps Unix commands to Windows equivalents (`mkdir`, `findstr`, `dir`, `move`, `del`, `copy`) and handles PowerShell distinction. Affects `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` only.

eli5.text: When you're using the software on a Windows computer, the assistant you interact with now gets a short note at the start of each conversation that explains how basic file commands work differently than on Mac or Linux. For example, it's told that you list files with 'dir' instead of 'ls', search inside files with 'findstr' instead of 'grep', and copy files with 'copy' instead of 'cp'. The note also tells the assistant to switch to PowerShell-style commands if you're using PowerShell. You wouldn't see this note directly, but if you're on Windows you might notice the assistant gives you more accurate tips when you ask it to run commands in your terminal.

ai.title: request-files-prompt.ts updates file reading heuristic
ai.summary: backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts adds two negative constraints to the file-reading heuristic. Follow-up requests and non-specific greetings now suppress new file reads. Change applies to the promptOpenAI call for request-files-prompt.ts. No user-facing surfaces affected.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to keep working on something you already started talking about, or just say hello without asking a real question, it now skips opening new files to look at. This only affects the behind-the-scenes step where the assistant decides whether it needs more files before answering, and nothing about how you see your answers changes. Today, follow-up questions and casual greetings get quick replies without extra file reading, while new, specific requests still pull in the files they need.

ai.title: Remove foundEndOfResponse flag from main-prompt stream handler
ai.summary:
Deleted `foundEndOfResponse` boolean and associated post-loop concatenation in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. The stream handler previously tracked whether `
[END]` appeared in printed chunks, then appended it back to `fullResponse` after the loop. The flag and its conditional append were redundant since the token is already stripped from user-visible output and `fullResponse` accumulates raw chunks directly. No behavioral change to chunk rendering or tool-call detection.

eli5.text: The assistant's reply system was doing extra bookkeeping to make sure the special end-of-reply marker never showed up twice in the recorded text, even though it was already being removed from what you see. That bookkeeping has been deleted, so the internal tracking that kept the duplicate from appearing is gone. You wouldn't notice anything different today. Nothing visible changed for you.

ai.title: Pass newFiles directly to getRelevantFileInfoMessage
ai.summary: getFileVersionUpdates in backend/src/main-prompt.ts now passes newFiles directly to getRelevantFileInfoMessage, removing the intermediate readFilesPaths array. The previous code mapped addedFiles to paths, but newFiles is already the correct format. No external behavior change.

eli5.text: When the system checks for updated information about new files you add, it now skips a no-longer-needed intermediate step and reads the necessary details directly from the file list you provided. This is purely an internal cleanup with no change to what you see or how things work. You wouldn't notice anything different today.
